title: NVIDIA RTX 5080 24 GB Launch May Be Delayed as Manufacturers Still Await Design Kits
summary: Nvidia RTX 5080 24GB launch may face delays as manufacturers await design kits
detailed: The launch of the NVIDIA RTX 5080 24 GB graphics card may be delayed beyond initial December or January expectations.
According to reports, NVIDIA has not yet delivered the necessary design kits to its main hardware partners during October as planned.
Without these design kits, manufacturers cannot begin mass production or accurately source components for a large-scale launch.
sentences: Just a few days ago, some rumors suggested that the RTX 5090 could be discontinued to make way for a possible RTX 5080 with 24 GB of memory .
However, although the new graphics card was expected to arrive soon, its launch may happen later than previously thought.
A new report shared by Benchlife suggests that this could be the case.
While December or January had been mentioned as possible launch dates for the graphics card, it now seems that it could take a little longer.
NVIDIA has apparently not yet provided the design kits to its partners.
According to the report , the company had planned to send these kits during October.
However, sources claim that NVIDIA has still not delivered them to its main partners.
This would make it almost impossible for the graphics card to launch within the dates that were initially leaked.
It is important to remember that graphics card manufacturers need enough time to work with these design kits.
In addition, if they do not know exactly which components they need to buy, this could delay mass production and make it harder to prepare enough graphics cards for a large-scale launch.
But most importantly, without these design kits, manufacturers cannot begin producing the graphics cards.
For this reason, the RTX 5080 24 GB launch now seems likely to be delayed.
At the moment, there is no new rumored release date, mainly because nobody knows when NVIDIA will provide the kits.
Once that happens, it will be possible to start talking about a possible launch date.
